newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Troubled S.African mines look north to Africa.
newsitem.headline: Troubled S.African mines look north to Africa.

text.p: Shrinking margins and tougher operating conditions were encouraging the move by South African mining houses into Africa, an international mining conference heard on Wednesday.

Fleming Martin Securities mining research director Dennis Tucker told the Investing in African Mining Conference the expansion into Africa by South African companies had been further encouraged by the country's transition to democracy and increased links with the rest of the world.
"The glorious days of announcing a new gold mining discovery (in South Africa) every other year have long come and gone," Tucker said.
Instead, lower grades were being mined and volumes were squeezed as mining activity moved deeper and further away from existing and often old infrastructure.
The industry had also been badly affected by the large number of public holidays, which had cut the average working period of about 71 shifts per quarter to about 68.
Management had tried to halt the decline in production but employee productivity "has failed to move off its low base," Tucker said.
The depreciation of the rand in 1996 increased mine revenues by 25 percent, but this had almost been wiped out by an average increase in production costs of around 20 percent.
"Clearly a margin squeeze is in the making yet again," he said.
The industry faced several other threats.
These included suggestions that mines should be made to amortise capital spending. If this happensd "deep level gold mining industry in South Africa is already history."
The new safety and health act would also make managing a deep level mine difficult while a range of new labour regulations could put further pressure on costs.
These were already under pressure because of the need to mine deeper.
"Last year's wage increase of some two percent above the ruling inflation rate sets the scene for an interesting wage battle this year, with inflation on the increase," Tucker said.
The industry would find it difficult to link wage increases to greater productivity with each mining house trying to negotiate its own deal.
On the operational front, mines were focusing more on ore reserve management and output this year was likely to match last year's 495 tonnes.

"Industry initiatives to access the remaining 40,000 tonnes of gold on the magnificent Witwatersrand may yet see the resurrection of South African gold output, but in the interim attention is focused north of South Africa," Tucker said. --Lynda Loxton, Cape Town newsroom +27 21 25-2238
